subject: Operations
title: Market Access Strategies
description: A 60-second lesson on Market Access Strategies.

hook.text: Starbucks has 35,000 stores in 80 countries. It didn't just export coffee—it adapted operations for every market.

buildup.text: Companies enter global markets through exporting, licensing, joint ventures, or wholly-owned subsidiaries.

discovery.text: Each mode trades off control, risk, and speed. Exporting is low-risk; full ownership is high-risk but high-control.

twist.text: McDonald's uses franchising in most countries but owns outlets in key markets—the entry mode matches the strategic need.

climax.text: The best global firms use different entry modes in different markets—one size never fits all.

punchline.text: Enter each market the way that market demands.

quiz.question: Why do companies use different entry modes in different markets?
options: Each market has different risks and opportunities
